en: The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of exactly 7,641 islands, with only about 2,000 of them being inhabited by people.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the sea.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers on the island of Luzon.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is the lowest active volcano in the Philippines, with its main crater situated only about 3 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer-long underground river that flows directly into the sea, making it one of the world's longest.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only about 85 to 160 millimeters in height and weighing 140 grams.
The Philippines is divided into 17 administrative regions, which are further subdivided into 81 provinces across its three main island groups.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the deepest point in the country, plunging to an impressive 10,540 meters below sea level.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, stretching approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Philippines has a total coastline of approximately 36,289 kilometers, giving it one of the longest coastlines of any country in the world.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of about 4,000 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the Philippines.
